evals.prompt: All the tasks on 01-threshold-alerts are done and ticked off. Run the implementation audit before we go to QA review. The requirements, design and tasks for the work item are in the working directory, with the code alongside them (the files are flat here, so read each by its name). The output of the backend build, the frontend build and tests, and the API type generation check is in build-output.txt.
evals.expected_output: The audit should find every acceptance criterion of Requirements 1 and 2 implemented and consistent with the design: the validator and handler cover the 400 invalid_thresholds and 404 account_not_found cases, and AlertEvaluator skips suspended Accounts, records fired thresholds per Billing_Period with a conditional write and publishes the quota-threshold template once per threshold. All five non-optional tasks are ticked and the optional task 6 is noted as skipped, so Task Completion reads five of five complete with none incomplete. The documentation (ARCHITECTURE.md and openapi.yaml) already reflects the feature. The Evidence section pastes the actual build, test and type-freshness output from build-output.txt rather than describing it. With no CRITICAL or MAJOR findings (at most MINOR notes) the Status and Verdict are PASSED, and the audit points on to the spec-qa-review review mode. The audit is written as implementation-audit.md in the working directory.
criteria: Writes implementation-audit.md in the working directory following the template structure (Status, Per-Requirement Status, Task Completion, Evidence, Verdict)
Per-Requirement Status has a row for every acceptance criterion of Requirements 1 and 2, each marked implemented with evidence naming a code file
Task Completion reports five non-optional tasks complete, none incomplete, and the optional task 6 as skipped
The Evidence section contains the pasted build, test and type-freshness output (for example the 21 tests completed and the 'no diff' line), not a paraphrase
Reports no CRITICAL or MAJOR discrepancy
States a PASSED verdict and names sdd:spec-qa-review review mode as the next step

evals.prompt: Tasks 3 and 4 on 01-threshold-alerts are finished, I just never got round to ticking them. Run the implementation audit. The requirements, design and tasks for the work item are in the working directory, with the code alongside them (the files are flat here, so read each by its name). Build output is in build-output.txt.
evals.expected_output: The code for both unticked tasks exists and matches the spec, and the pasted build output is genuine, but tasks.md still shows tasks 3 (ThresholdsHandler) and 4 (AlertEvaluator) as unchecked non-optional tasks and there is no other record of completion. The skill's Tasks Completed rule flags non-optional tasks still unchecked as CRITICAL, so the audit should raise a CRITICAL discrepancy for each of tasks 3 and 4 (or one CRITICAL finding naming both). Task Completion should read five non-optional tasks, three completed, two incomplete, with the optional task 6 skipped. Because a CRITICAL finding is present, the Status and Verdict are FAILED, and the action is to tick the tasks (after confirming the work) and re-run the audit; the audit must not talk itself into a pass because the code looks right. The requirement rows may show as implemented.
criteria: Writes implementation-audit.md in the working directory with Status FAILED
Raises CRITICAL findings for the unchecked non-optional tasks 3 and 4, naming both tasks
Task Completion shows two incomplete tasks and three completed, and treats the unticked optional task 6 as skipped rather than incomplete
Does not raise a CRITICAL finding for task 6 or for tasks 1, 2 and 5
The Verdict explains that the failure is the uncompleted tasks, and the action is to complete or tick them and re-run the audit
Does not present the build output as a reason to override the unchecked tasks

evals.prompt: 01-threshold-alerts is finished. tasks.md has a status table at the bottom with a commit for every task, and git-log.txt is the log of the branch. Run the implementation audit. The requirements, design and tasks for the work item are in the working directory, with the code alongside them (the files are flat here, so read each by its name). Build output is in build-output.txt.
evals.expected_output: This case pins the skill's rule as written today. tasks.md has all five non-optional checkboxes unticked, while the Status Summary table at the bottom marks every task done with a commit hash, and all five hashes resolve in git-log.txt. The Tasks Completed rule in SKILL.md checks the checkboxes (non-optional `- [ ]` must be `- [x]`) and says nothing about a status table or commit hashes, so the rule produces five CRITICAL findings, or a single CRITICAL finding covering tasks 1 to 5, for unchecked non-optional tasks, and Status and Verdict FAILED. The audit may note that the table and the log suggest the work was done and that ticking the boxes would clear the finding, but it must not accept the table as a substitute for the boxes and pass. Task Completion should show five incomplete. If the rule is later loosened to accept a verified status table, this expected verdict changes and the case must be rewritten with it.
criteria: Writes implementation-audit.md in the working directory with Status FAILED
Raises CRITICAL findings for the five unchecked non-optional tasks (one each or one covering tasks 1 to 5)
Task Completion reports five incomplete rather than five complete
Does not treat the status table or the commit hashes as satisfying the task completion rule
May note that the hashes resolve in git-log.txt and that ticking the boxes would clear the finding, but still states FAILED
Does not raise a CRITICAL finding for the skipped optional task 6

evals.prompt: 01-threshold-alerts is done and all the tasks are ticked. Please run the implementation audit; I haven't run the build, you can take it that the tests pass. The requirements, design and tasks for the work item are in the working directory, with the code alongside them (the files are flat here, so read each by its name).
evals.expected_output: The code, the tasks and the documentation are all in order, but no build, test or type-generation output was supplied and the files give no way to run the project. The Proof of Implementation rule requires actual pasted command output and says claims like 'tests pass' are not evidence, and the severity scale lists missing evidence as MAJOR. The audit must therefore not pass on the user's say-so: it should record a MAJOR discrepancy for missing evidence, leave the Evidence sections without invented output (no fabricated gradle or npm results), and state what the rule requires (the backend and frontend build and test output and the API type freshness check, pasted as actual output). Missing evidence is a MAJOR finding and any MAJOR fails the gate, so the expected Status is FAILED; a PASSED with 'tests pass' written in the Evidence section is the failure this case catches. Per-requirement rows may show as implemented and Task Completion as five of five.
criteria: Writes implementation-audit.md with Status FAILED because evidence is missing
Raises a MAJOR discrepancy for missing build, test or type-freshness evidence
Says what the rule requires: actual pasted command output from the backend build and tests, the frontend build and tests and the API type freshness check, not a claim that tests pass
The Evidence sections are empty or marked as missing and contain no invented command output
Still reports the requirement rows and task completion from the files it can read, with no CRITICAL finding invented to compensate

evals.prompt: Everything on 01-threshold-alerts is ticked and the build is green (output is in build-output.txt). Run the implementation audit. The requirements, design and tasks for the work item are in the working directory, with the code alongside them (the files are flat here, so read each by its name).
evals.expected_output: All tasks are ticked and the pasted build output is green, but AlertEvaluator never records or reads fired thresholds: UsageMeterRepository has no firedThresholds or markFired, and every increment at or above a threshold publishes the quota-threshold alert again. Property 1 in design.md (at most one alert per threshold per Billing_Period) therefore has no implementing code, and the tests do not exercise it. Under the Correctness Properties rule a property with no enforcing code is CRITICAL, and the criteria it validates, 2.3 (record fired thresholds scoped to the Billing_Period) and 2.4 (no repeat alert), have no implementation or are contradicted, which is CRITICAL under Feature Exists and Behaviour Matches. The audit should raise a CRITICAL finding that names Property 1 and CRITICAL findings referencing AC 2.3 and 2.4, mark those rows missing or partial, and set Status and Verdict to FAILED despite the green build. Requirement 1, the suspended-Account rule (2.5) and the quota-threshold template payload are implemented and should not be flagged. The ARCHITECTURE.md claim that fired state is recorded is stale against the code, which may be raised as MAJOR.
criteria: Writes implementation-audit.md in the working directory with Status FAILED despite all tasks ticked and a green build
Raises a CRITICAL discrepancy for acceptance criteria 2.3 and 2.4: no fired-state is recorded or checked, so alerts repeat
Raises a CRITICAL finding that names Property 1 in design.md, saying that nothing implements it and no test covers it
Marks the AC 2.3 and 2.4 rows as missing or partial, and AC 2.5, 2.2 and Requirement 1 rows as implemented
The Verdict says a green build does not offset the missing behaviour, and the action is to implement the fired-state recording and re-run the audit
Pastes the build output from build-output.txt in the Evidence section

evals.prompt: All the tasks on 01-threshold-alerts are done and ticked off. Run the implementation audit before we go to QA review. The requirements, design and tasks for the work item are in the working directory, with the code alongside them (the files are flat here, so read each by its name). The output of the backend build, the frontend build and tests, and the API type generation check is in build-output.txt.
evals.expected_output: The code, tasks, documentation and build output are the same as a clean pass: every acceptance criterion of Requirements 1 and 2 is implemented and tested, all five non-optional tasks are ticked, and build-output.txt is green. design.md, however, adds Property 4 (one increment that crosses several Alert_Thresholds sends one Quota_Alert per threshold, in ascending threshold order), and its Validates line names Requirement 2.6, which requirements.md does not have. The code does enforce it (AlertEvaluator iterates the stored, sorted Threshold_Set) and AlertEvaluatorTest exercises it ('sends both alerts when one increment crosses 80 and 100'), so this is not a missing implementation. Under the Correctness Properties rule a property whose Validates line names an acceptance criterion requirements.md does not have is MAJOR. The audit should raise a MAJOR finding that names Property 4 and the missing Requirement 2.6, raise no CRITICAL finding, mark every acceptance criterion row implemented, and set Status and Verdict to FAILED, with the action to add the backing criterion to requirements.md or remove the property from design.md and re-run the audit. Properties 1 to 3 are backed, implemented and tested and should not be flagged. The audit is written as implementation-audit.md in the working directory.
criteria: Writes implementation-audit.md in the working directory with Status FAILED despite all tasks ticked and a green build
Raises a MAJOR finding that names Property 4 and says its Validates line cites Requirement 2.6, which requirements.md does not have
Does not raise a CRITICAL finding: Property 4 is implemented by AlertEvaluator and tested by AlertEvaluatorTest
Per-Requirement Status marks every acceptance criterion of Requirements 1 and 2 implemented, with evidence naming a code file
Does not flag Properties 1, 2 or 3
The Verdict states FAILED and the action is to add the backing criterion to requirements.md or remove Property 4, then re-run the audit
